Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion and helpful context on Skybridge's two product lines. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can converge on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and get you a realistic dedicated-sizing proposal: 

Ask summary (from call):
- Primary apps: conversational search (low latency) + batch enrichment jobs (throughput-focused).
- Current observed averages: ~18 TPS (conversational), but spikes up to ~120 TPS for short windows.
- Typical prompt length: ~350 tokens; long-form customers can push ~2k tokens in rarer flows.
- Mix of model sizes: 8k context for most queries; a smaller portion uses 32k context for long transcripts.
- Security: SOC2 and VPC peering required for Prod; may consider Private/on-prem for regulated tenants.

What we recommend as immediate outputs: 
1) Dedicated sizing worksheet (attached) — please fill the shaded columns with your real traffic shape and token distribution so we can model concurrency & batching.
2) Short follow-up workshop (60 min) with your infra lead to confirm SLA targets, burst patterns, and any isolation needs (VPC, per-tenant pools).
3) Our initial guidance: plan for a hybrid dedicated pool (H100-class for low-latency gen, A100-tier for cheaper multiplexed batch workers) OR a Dedicated-only H100 pool if latency is the primary constraint. We can refine after we see the workbook.

Next steps I propose: 
- You fill the attached workbook and return by EOD Fri 7/30.
- We run an internal sizing sketch and then schedule a 60-min sizing workshop the week of 8/2.

Attachments: skybridge_capacity_workbook.xlsx (workbook, shaded inputs), sample_token_profile.csv (example token distribution).

If that plan looks good I can loop in Solutions Engineering for the workshop and draft a preliminary SKU/ballpark commitment.

Thanks — talk soon,

Alex / Maya — quick take from ops/architecture on the GPU-family question so you have a concrete framing before the workshop:

Short answer: H100 for latency-critical real-time gen; A100 for mixed workloads where cost efficiency matters; L4s are attractive for massively parallel cheap inference but generally not a great fit for large-context (32k) models.

Sizing guidance (rough):
- For 18 TPS sustained (350 tokens avg) + 120 TPS spikes, and a mix of 8k/32k models, a blended pool with one H100 slab sized for the 95th p95 latency workload (front of house) + 2–3 A100 nodes for multiplexed batch/backfill tends to be the most economical starting point.
- Concurrency: target 6–12 concurrent requests per A100 worker for 350-token generative prompts with batching enabled; H100 can operate at lower batch sizes to preserve latency (concurrency 2–4).
- Burst handling: Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity via reserved burst slots and cross-pool spillover; typical warm-up for adding a new slab ~2–4 minutes depending on image/container cache state — if you need sub-minute scaling we recommend pre-warmed burst slots.

We'll convert this into a few concrete SKU scenarios (cost/latency tradeoffs) once we get the workbook numbers. Happy to present these in the workshop.
